name: Inverse-time characteristic qualifier
summary: Qualifier showing that a measuring relay's operating time falls as the measured quantity rises above its setting.
description: The inverse-time qualifier marks a measuring element whose operating time depends on how far the measured quantity exceeds the setting: the larger the overcurrent, the faster the trip. On drawings it appears with overcurrent and earth-fault elements that are graded against fuses and downstream relays.

The qualifier does not name the curve. Standard inverse, very inverse and extremely inverse curves grade very differently, and the curve type, time multiplier and pick-up current must be taken from the protection settings.
readingNotes: Identify the curve type from the settings record.
Read with the grading study for the feeder.
distinction: An inverse-time qualifier marks a current-dependent delay; a definite-time qualifier marks a fixed delay.
